summary: Frontend E2E test of new AreaScan tick-instant / untick-undo behaviour on /area-scan/<areaId>. Seeded 4 temp ZZ equipment (all assigned to a temp ZZ staff m1 with PIN 2468) in facility Factorty › Ground Floor › Finished Goods, and pre-ticked e4 as admin via POST /api/maintenance/area-scan/{areaId}/tick to simulate 'ticked by another actor'. Fresh browser context → /area-scan/<id> shows StaffScanLogin, picked staff m1, PIN 2468, signed in. area-scan-page loaded with header hint 'Tick = saved instantly.' visible, no 'Mark N as Maintenance Complete' button, no remarks textarea. Summary chips read '4 due / 1 done' (admin's pre-tick counted). e4 (admin-ticked) row correctly shows Done badge with green CheckCircle icon and NO checkbox (data-testid area-eq-check-<id> absent) — cannot be undone by this staff. Clicking area-eq-check-<e1> → briefly busy → row flips to state=done, text 'Saved ✓ by ZZ Tick Staff · HH:MM · untick to undo', checkbox checked; summary updates to '3 due / 2 done'; Mongo maintenance_records doc created with performed_via='area_qr', performed_by='ZZ Tick Staff'. Clicking same checkbox again → untick → row back to 'Due today', unchecked; summary reverts to '4 due / 1 done'; Mongo record deleted and maintenance_audit doc with action='area_qr_undo' written. area-tick-all button visible with label 'Tick all due (4)' (>=2 tickable); clicking it saved all 4, all rows show Done, summary '0 due / 5 done', tick-all button no longer visible. All temp ZZ equipment/staff/records/slots/audits/sessions cleaned up post-test.
critical_code_review_comments: Same observation as iteration_352: unassigned equipment (empty maintenance_staff) remains tickable by any signed-in staff on the area page. During Tick all due, the shared area's existing 'FG Conveyor' (unassigned) also got ticked by our temp staff; had to be rolled back manually. If policy is 'only assigned staff can tick', tighten _tickable to require the actor be in assigned_staff (admin still bypass).

Optimistic tick updates state to state='done' + record.completed_at=r.record.completed_at — code assumes tick response returns { performed_by, record: { completed_at } }. Backend contract works, but frontend also fires load() on catch which is good defensive UX.
